answer: In an agent marketplace buying pigment for a terrace mural, each trading identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can submit bids. A thousand fake identities therefore tie up $100,000 across that month-long horizon, even if none wins work. Creating keys remains cheap, but multiplying eligible bidders requires proportional capital: the attacker must fund every bond and forgo other uses of that money until release.
